subject: MAP: perf gating checklist & load-window coordination
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Wu <jamie@datacraft.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-11T08:14:00Z
Subject: MAP: perf gating checklist & load-window coordination

Jamie —

Great to meet on the call yesterday. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) we promised a short, executable performance playbook so DataCraft can validate latency, throughput and TTFT under a production-like pattern before signing the committed capacity. I sketched the gating criteria below and attached a draft checklist: MAP_perf_checklist_v1.xlsx.

Proposed perf targets for the evaluation (can iterate):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): < 150ms (p50) for single-stream interactive workloads
- Latency: p95 < 350ms for 512-token responses under target concurrency
- Throughput: sustained 350 req/s aggregate for the test model (burst to 500 req/s for cold-start window)
- Concurrency: validate up to 64 concurrent sessions with KV cache warmed for steady-state runs

Logistics we need from you to finalize the windows:
1) Confirm three candidate 4-hour load windows (preferred: US mornings 9am–1pm PT)
2) Provide a list of representative prompt families + sample doc sets (we can use the ones you shared but please mark any restricted samples)
3) Confirm whether you want data plane traffic over VPC peering or via our test public endpoints (we'll provide temporary keys either way)

Next steps from our side: Karthik will provision test accounts and a small dedicated fleet for the reserved windows; Monica will own the automated test harness and the runbook. I'll attach pass/fail criteria to the MAP and drive scheduling once we have your windows.

Attachments: MAP_perf_checklist_v1.xlsx

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Wu <jamie@datacraft.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@datacraft.io>
Date: 2027-03-11T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: perf gating checklist & load-window coordination

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 08:14 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jamie —
> 
> Great to meet on the call yesterday. Per our mutual action plan (MAP) we promised a short, executable performance playbook...

Thanks, Priyom — this is exactly what we need. Quick answers:
- Candidate windows: Mar 24 09:00–13:00 PT, Mar 26 10:00–14:00 PT, Apr 1 08:00–12:00 PT (we prefer earlier in the day)
- Prompt families: sending a separate S3 link with the masked test corpus (ops@datacraft.io will follow up)
- Networking: we prefer VPC peering for the most accurate network profile; we can provide a peering contact if you need it.

Key ask before we lock the windows: we need test accounts/keys and any ephemeral certs documented. Also include the exact pass/fail criteria in the MAP before execution so procurement can greenlight the pilot.

Samir (ops) — I'll drop the corpus link and availability calendar to you.

Best,
Jamie
Head of Platform Reliability, DataCraft
jamie@datacraft.io

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-11T14:30:00Z
Subject: Fwd: MAP: perf gating checklist & load-window coordination

Karthik / Monica — forwarding DataCraft's windows and asks. Please action:
- Karthik: provision three test API keys (scoped: testing only, rate-limited) and create a short readme with endpoints + expected request shapes. Place keys into test_accounts_keys_v2.txt (stub attached).
- Monica: can you script the steady-state run (64 concurrent streams) with our harness and include scripts to capture TTFT + p95 latency histograms? We should also include a cold-start burst run.

Notes on environment: DataCraft prefers VPC peering. If peering isn't possible, reserve a public test endpoint and capture network jitter metrics. Also confirm whether we should enable prefix caching for their runs (recommended).

I'll loop in infra if we need a temporary dedicated fleet. Plan to push the final MAP doc to the Drive link and share a HubSpot note.

Attachments: test_accounts_keys_v2.txt (placeholder)

Thanks,
Priyom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-12T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP: perf gating checklist & load-window coordination

Priyom —

I created three scoped API keys and a test tenant in our staging VPC for DataCraft. Details (high level):
- Keys: dc-test-1, dc-test-2, dc-test-3 (see test_accounts_keys_v2.txt for the key IDs; secrets delivered in 1Password shared folder)
- Networking: requested VPC peering; if not approved in time we'll provide public endpoints with a temporary TLS cert and a bastion for SSH access to the test harness host.
- Fleet: reserved 4 x A5000-equivalent GPUs for each scheduled 4-hour window (enough to hit 350 req/s sustained per spec)
- Telemetry: added an S3 bucket for raw logs and enabled token-level tracing for the runs (retention 30 days)

Attach: load_window_availability.ics with the three windows Jamie proposed. Monica, I left the prefix cache off by default — you can toggle in the harness; let's capture both cache-off and cache-on runs for comparison.

If DataCraft requires peering contacts, send me their peering CIDR & account id and I'll escalate.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Wu <jamie@datacraft.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@datacraft.io>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-12T18:41:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: perf gating checklist & load-window coordination

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the speed. Confirming the Mar 24 window as our first preference. Couple of clarifying points before we kick off: 
- Pass/fail criteria: can you add an explicit row in the MAP that calls out 'acceptable variance' (e.g., p95 latency must not exceed target by more than 15% during 80% of the run window)? We need that language for procurement sign-off.
- Auditing: we'll need a short delivery of the audit log samples (anonymized) after the run for our security review.
- DocuSign / MSA: procurement asked for a one-pager summarizing the pilot scope and liability — is that something Redwood can produce this week?

If those look good we'll confirm Mar 24 09:00–13:00 PT. I'll share the masked corpus link to ops@datacraft.io and drop the peering CIDR by EOD.

—Jamie

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Wu <jamie@datacraft.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-13T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: perf gating checklist & load-window coordination — final

Jamie / Team —

All good. I've updated the MAP with the explicit pass/fail language and attached MAP_perf_checklist_v1.xlsx (final draft) to this thread. Summary of agreed items:
- Window: Mar 24, 09:00–13:00 PT (confirmed)
- Keys: dc-test-1..3, delivered via 1Password; scope: test-only, rate limits applied
- Environment: staging VPC peering requested; public fallback available if peering not approved
- Test plan: cold-start burst, steady-state (64 concurrent streams), cache-off/cache-on comparison, telemetry capture (TTFT + p95 histograms + request logs)
- Pass/fail: p95 latency must remain ≤ 15% above the MAP target for ≥ 80% of the steady-state window; TTFT median must be ≤ 150ms
- Deliverables: anonymized audit log samples, run summary report (latency/throughput/TTFT + anomalies), post-mortem if any threshold is missed

Attachments: MAP_perf_checklist_v1.xlsx (final), load_window_availability.ics (calendar invite created), test_accounts_keys_v2.txt (key IDs; secrets in 1Password)

I'll create the HubSpot note and attach the Drive MAP. Monica/karthik — please confirm when the harness is green and we can do a dry run earlier in the week (short 30-min smoke).

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri@redwood.ai
